BILL NUMBER:  S3329

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the public service law, in relation to transfer of
franchises or stocks


 PURPOSE OF THE BILL :
This bill would expand the types of business entities that must obtain
Public Service Commission (PSC) approval for the transfer of
franchises or stocks of electric, gas, water, steam and telephone
corporations.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :
Sections 1, 2, 3 and 4 of this bill amend Public Service Law (PSL) §§
70 (gas corporations and electric corporations), 83 (steam
corporations), 89-h (water corporations) and 100 (telephone
corporations), respectively, to expand the PSC's jurisdiction over
transfers of franchises or stocks to include companies, associations,
partnerships and other business entities that propose to acquire such
franchises or stocks.

Section 5 of this bill provides for an immediate effective date.

 EXISTING LAW :
PSL §§70, 83, 89-h and 100 establish requirements for the transfer of
franchises and stocks of electric, gas, steam, water or telephone
corporations, respectively. Such provisions generally prohibit the
transfer or lease of franchises or stocks to stock corporations
without PSC review and approval.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
This is a new proposal.

 STATEMENT IN SUPPORT :
The PSL provides that the PSC must approve any transfer of franchises
or stock of electric, gas, steam, water or telephone corporations to
stock corporations.  However, entities formed as partnerships, limited
liability companies and associations, as well as other business
entities that are not stock corporations, do not fall within the
purview of the franchise/stock acquisition provisions of the PSL.
Therefore, the PSC dues not have jurisdiction over acquisitions of
stock by and transfers of franchises to such entities as they are not
"stock corporations."

This lack of jurisdiction could result in a transfer of control of a
utility company, and possibly detrimental consequences to the utility
and its customers, particularly where the interests of shareholders,
partners or members might not coincide with those of the utility and
utility customers. The reliability of the various utility systems is
integral to the personal and economic needs of the residential and
commercial utility customers in this State. It is essential that the
PSC continue to review proposals to transfer stock or franchises to
ensure that purchasers have the experience and ability to maintain
utility systems in a safe and reliable manner and provide service at
just and reasonable rates.

This bill closes this loophole by providing PSC with jurisdiction to
review and determine whether stock acquisitions over a ten per centum
threshold by all business entities should be approved This expanded
jurisdiction is thus consistent with PSC's mandate to ensure that such
transfer is in the public interest and that safe and reliable utility
service is provided at just and reasonable rates.

 BUDGET IMPLICATIONS :
None.
 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Immediately.

summary: Relates to the transfer of franchises or stocks by gas corporations, electric corporations, steam corporations, water-works corporations, telegraph corporations and telephone corporations.
title: Relates to the transfer of franchises or stocks by certain public service corporations
